source.quoted_text: Sch I Art. 39 (both columns, IGR text): 'MEMORANDUM OF ASSOCIATION OF A COMPANY — (a) if accompanied by articles of association under section 26 of the Companies Act, 1956 — One thousand rupees; (b) if not so accompanied — 0.2 per cent according to the share capital of the company, subject to minimum of rupees one thousand and maximum of rupees 50,00,000.'

pending_verification.reason: Whether the memorandum is accompanied by articles of association changes the charge from a flat amount to an ad-valorem amount. Require an explicit yes/no answer; a missing fact cannot default to the higher branch silently.

notes_for_reviewer: CONFIDENCE: HIGH (official IGR text). The Maharashtra CAP showcase (PRD §5.2 — caps are load-bearing and a differentiator): MOA not accompanied by AoA → 0.2% of share_capital, floor Rs 1,000, CAP Rs 50,00,000. accompanied_by_aoa='yes' → flat Rs 1,000. Instrument key memorandum_of_association is outside the MVP-15 but encoded to exercise the cap primitive; harmless (validator warns, non-blocking). Could be dropped if the founder prefers strict MVP-15 scope.

source.ref: Maharashtra Stamp Act, 1958, Sch. I Art. 48(a)-(e),(h) (Rs 500 subst. for Rs 100 by Mah. 20 of 2015)
source.quoted_text: Sch I Art. 48 (both columns, IGR text): 'POWER OF ATTORNEY not being a Proxy — (a) sole purpose of procuring registration ... single transaction — Five hundred rupees; (b) suits under Presidency Small Cause Courts Act — Five hundred rupees; (c) authorising one or more persons to act in a single transaction other than (a) — Five hundred rupees; (d) authorising one person to act in more than one transaction or generally — Five hundred rupees; (e) authorising more than one person ... jointly or severally or generally — Five hundred rupees; (h) in any other case — Five hundred rupees for each person authorised.' Maharashtra Act XX of 2015 s.20(25) substitutes Rs 500 for Rs 100 and was first published on 24-Apr-2015; the IGR consolidated footnote separately states 24-May-2015, so the exact boundary remains pending human legal review. Clause (f)(i): for consideration authorising sale of immovable property — same duty as Conveyance (Art 25) on market value. Clause (f)(ii)(a): to sell/transfer without consideration to father/mother/brother/sister/wife/husband/daughter/son/grandson/granddaughter or spouse's such relatives — Rs 500; else (f)(ii)(b) — Conveyance rate. Clause (g): to a promoter/developer for construction/development/sale/transfer — Conveyance rate (s.32A applies; Rs 100 if proper duty paid under Art 5(g-a) agreement between same parties).

pending_verification.reason: The flat Article 48 amount is returned only for clauses (a)-(e), derived from observable document-purpose answers. Sale/transfer powers, developer/promoter powers, clause (h), another purpose, or uncertainty remain outside this flat rule.

notes_for_reviewer: CONFIDENCE: HIGH for clauses (a)-(e) = Rs 500 (official IGR). The shared input contract derives the fixed scope from document purpose and explicit absence of immovable-transfer and developer/promoter powers; callers cannot assert the legal conclusion. Clause (h) is deliberately refused because its Rs 500-per-person arithmetic is not represented by this flat rule. ESCALATIONS: clause (f) POA for consideration to sell immovable → Conveyance rate on market value; (f)(ii)(a) family gift-POA → Rs 500; (g) developer/promoter POA → Conveyance rate. effective_from 2015-05-24 = the Rs 100→Rs 500 change; the pre-2015 Rs 100 version is a back-catalogue item (M2).
